facts: The Vault (/vault) is MotoPass's proof archive — it shows Bitcoin-anchored proofs for all 50 programs.
The Vault also hosts the Document Stamper — members can timestamp their own files on Bitcoin.
Document stamping works by hashing the file locally (SHA-256), then submitting only the hash to the Satohash API.
The file never leaves the member's device — only the 64-character hex hash is sent to Satohash.
The shared document registry (localStorage key 'motopass-vault-documents') is the single source of truth across Profile, Vault, and Dashboard.
A stamped document has three honest statuses: pending (submitted, awaiting Bitcoin block), confirmed (anchor seen at block N), error (submission failed, retry available).
Only confirmed stamps (with a Bitcoin block height) are treated as proofs — pending stamps are not proof of anything yet.
Members can re-check any document's anchor status via the Satohash API (GET /api/stamps/:id).
Members can retry-stamp a failed document — the file is never needed again, only the already-local hash is re-submitted.
The Apply flow (/apply) lets members attach confirmed document stamps to their application — only Bitcoin-confirmed stamps are selectable.
When attaching documents to an application, the on-chain claim is 'these exact files existed at block N' — never 'this person is X'.
The document registry can be exported as a portable JSON backup with verify links — so the backup can be audited against Bitcoin without MotoPass.
Registry backups can be restored via the import UI — it validates the schema, checks hash format, and merges into the existing registry.
The Verify tool (/verify) lets members generate a hash from their own data and stamp it independently.
Proof cards in the Vault show: block number, last-checked date, content hash, OTS receipt path, and education tooltips explaining each item.
The Vault's education section explains the 4-step proof workflow: hash → stamp → verify → apply.
Profile (/profile) shows the same document registry as Vault — stamp from either place, same list everywhere.
Dashboard shows a document registry card with stamp/re-check quick actions — the complete doc lifecycle is visible at a glance.
Satohash verify URLs are allowlisted — Paige must never fabricate or alter verify links.
The Vault credential export bundles program proofs (not documents) as a portable JSON — separate from the document registry export.

stamp_file: 1. Member drops a file (passport scan, contract, application, creative work) into the Document Stamper
2. SHA-256 computed locally via crypto.subtle — the file never leaves the device
3. Hash posted to Satohash API (POST /api/stamp) with filename metadata
4. Light poll for Bitcoin anchor (GET /api/stamps/:id, 3 attempts, 2s interval)
5. Status determined: pending (no block yet), confirmed (block_height present), error (API failure)
6. Registry entry saved to localStorage with metadata + hash only, never the file
attach_to_application: 1. Member visits /apply and sees the 'Attach stamped documents' card
2. Registry is loaded — only Bitcoin-confirmed stamps are selectable
3. Pending/error rows show honest labels (Awaiting anchor / Stamp error) and are disabled
4. ?proof=<hash> deep-link auto-selects a matching confirmed registry doc
5. On submit, doc hashes are included in the stamped payload and docProofs stored on the application
6. Success card lists attached proofs with Satohash verify links
verify_independently: 1. Copy hash or proof URL from any program card or document entry
3. Satohash shows whether hash is anchored and at which Bitcoin block
export_restore: 1. Export: Download motopass-documents-<BUILD>.json with all registry entries + verify URLs
2. Restore: Import button validates schema, checks 64-hex hash format, merges into registry
3. Post-restore: Re-check all confirms anchors against Satohash API

honesty_rules: Only confirmed stamps (with bitcoin_block_height) are proofs — pending is 'awaiting anchor', not proof.
The file never leaves the device — only the SHA-256 hash is sent to Satohash.
The on-chain claim is 'this exact file existed at block N' — never identity claims.
Verify URLs are allowlisted — never fabricate or alter satohash.io/verify links.
Badge vocabulary: Demo / Proof on file / Bitcoin-verified. Never invent categories.
Do not fabricate block numbers — only cite bitcoin_block_height from the API.
The registry is device-local (localStorage) — it doesn't sync across devices without export/import.

badge_vocabulary.Demo: seed/placeholder proof for testing — NOT verification
badge_vocabulary.Proof on file: a recorded proof URL exists — verify before relying
badge_vocabulary.Bitcoin-verified: hash is anchored on Bitcoin via Satohash/OTS
badge_vocabulary.Re-anchoring: proof being re-stamped after data update; converges on next daily sweep
badge_vocabulary.Awaiting anchor: document stamp submitted but no Bitcoin block yet — not proof
badge_vocabulary.Stamp error: submission failed; retry available via restamp or Satohash stamp guide

member_scripts.what_is_vault: The Vault is your proof archive — it shows Bitcoin-anchored proofs for all 50 countries and lets you timestamp your own documents the same way.
member_scripts.how_to_stamp: Drop any file into the Document Stamper on /vault. Its fingerprint (hash) is computed locally — the file never leaves your device — and anchored to Bitcoin via Satohash. You get a proof card showing the block number when it's confirmed.
member_scripts.is_it_safe: Your file never leaves your device. Only the cryptographic fingerprint (SHA-256 hash) is sent to Satohash. Even Satohash never sees your document — just the hash.
member_scripts.how_to_verify: Copy the hash from any proof card, open satohash.io/verify/<hash>, and see for yourself. You don't need to trust MotoPass.
member_scripts.what_can_i_stamp: Anything you want a tamper-evident record of: passport scans, contracts, proof-of-funds, applications, wills, creative works, research notes.
member_scripts.how_to_attach: When you apply on /apply, you can attach confirmed document stamps to your application. Only Bitcoin-confirmed stamps are selectable — pending stamps aren't proof yet.
member_scripts.how_to_export: Download your document registry as a portable JSON backup from the Dashboard or Profile. It includes verify links so you can audit against Bitcoin without MotoPass.
member_scripts.how_to_restore: Use the Import button on the Dashboard or Profile to restore a backup. It validates the format and merges into your existing registry.

pages./vault: Proof archive + Document Stamper + OTS verifier + program proof cards
